content.text:
It’s a frontend URL-handling bug, not a missing Social Radar page.

The notification contains this valid absolute URL:

`https://app.lobu.ai/buremba/agents/personal-agent/behaviors/71`

But the client router treats it as relative and constructs:

`.../lobu-builder/chat/https:/app.lobu.ai/buremba/agents/personal-agent/behaviors/71`

That malformed path produces the 404. Opening the intended URL directly works and shows Behavior 71’s activity.

The mismatch is between [activity-links.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/owletto/src/lib/activity-links.ts:1), which assumes app-relative URLs, and [home-attention-timeline.tsx](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/owletto/src/components/home/home-attention-timeline.tsx:136), which passes the parsed result to the router.

Workaround: open [Social Radar directly](https://app.lobu.ai/buremba/agents/personal-agent/behaviors/71).

I only diagnosed it; no code was changed. The proper fix is to normalize same-origin absolute notification URLs before routing, covering existing stored notifications too.

content.text:
Fixed and verified in production.

The cause was an absolute `resource_url` stored by Social Radar. The UI treated it as relative, creating a malformed nested URL and a 404.

- Social Radar v9 now emits relative app URLs.
- The frontend normalizes legacy absolute URLs, so existing notifications also work.
- Merged [Owletto #683](https://github.com/lobu-ai/owletto/pull/683) and [Lobu #2434](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2434).
- Production is healthy on merge `22b421ab`; both replicas are ready.
- Live-clicked an old affected notification: it opened Behavior 71’s run history with no 404.
- 1,145 Owletto tests, builds, required CI, and Opus review passed.
- Worktree, branches, browser sessions, and temporary files were cleaned up; temp files are recoverable from Trash.
